newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Industry council wants action to promote SMEs.
newsitem.headline: Industry council wants action to promote SMEs.

text.p: European Union industry ministers called on member states on Thursday to take action to help promote small firms, seen as vital in the Union's efforts to reduce its high jobless rate.
The resolution on "realising the full potential of small and medium-sized enterprises" states that such firms play an important role in terms of growth and the creation of new jobs.
"SMEs make a vital contribution to job creation and competitiveness within the European Union," the resolution said.

"The further development of SMEs is of great importance to economic growth, regional development and social cohesion in the European Union," it added, recognising that there were several "inhibitors" which restrict growth and job creation in SMEs.
"SMEs face a complex business environment...there is a need to reduce the administrative burden for entrepreneurs and to simplify rules in force," the resolution said.

It calls on member states and the Commission to give "concrete and practical recognition of the particular role which small and micro-enterprises play in the generation and maintenance of employment in the European Union and to the particular difficulties of these size categories of enterprise arising from the burden imposed by a complex business environment."

For example, the text says EU countries and the Commission should promote targeted administrative and regulatory simplification and address the needs of small firms in the transition to a single currency.
They should also improve access of small firms to EU programmes and structural funds and boost local development and employment initiatives.

It said total administrative costs for SMEs remained high and that the formalities associated with setting up new enterprises were a cause of concern. Small firms also have difficulties accessing external finance.

The resolution also calls on the Commission to improve access of SMEs to venture capital, to encourage SMEs in creating or developing activities in another member state as well as to improve access of SMEs to EU research and technical development programmes.
The resolution responds to the Commission's communication presented in July last year on an Integrated Programme for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises and the Craft Sector.
